findings.title: Malformed provider envelopes and invalid UTF-8 escape named failure boundaries
findings.trigger: Mock the existing URL transport with b'null' or b'\xff'; do not contact a provider.
findings.observed: Raw AttributeError/TypeError/UnicodeDecodeError; Jev evaluate returns no refused evaluation.
findings.expected: DeepSeek names a provider protocol failure; Jev returns a refused advisory evaluation so the scientific turn continues.
findings.suggested_minimal_change: Validate mapping envelopes and wrap UnicodeDecodeError/JSON/envelope violations with provider-specific protocol errors; retain transport retry policy.
findings.limits: Synthetic malformed responses; no incidence estimate or actual live outage is claimed.

findings.title: Provider-reported usage is omitted when completion text is unusable
findings.trigger: A response has content=null, finish_reason=length and usage={prompt_tokens:7,completion_tokens:3,total_tokens:10}.
findings.observed: LLMProtocolError is raised, but provider_usage is {calls:0} with no token usage.
findings.expected: Received provider-reported usage remains available even when content cannot be used.
findings.suggested_minimal_change: Record validated provider usage before text interpretation; distinguish attempted, received and usable calls.
findings.limits: This establishes omitted reported tokens, not the monetary billing of a live request.

findings.title: Within-round duplicate suppression depends on persistent reuse
findings.trigger: Dispatch two requests with identical model inputs, different tracking IDs, two workers and reuse_predictions=False.
findings.observed: Two backend predictions; the reuse-enabled control has one.
findings.expected: The dispatcher's documented once-per-distinct-input round property is independent of cross-round caching.
findings.suggested_minimal_change: Rebind completed results from a temporary per-round key map; preserve original provenance, abstentions and compute accounting.
findings.limits: Measured call counts use a synthetic counting backend; no production speedup or wall-time estimate is claimed.

findings.title: Repeated typed judgments merge served versions under the first model
findings.trigger: Two evaluations of the same state return models jev-version-1/jev-version-2 with p=0.1/0.9.
findings.observed: Aggregated p=0.5 is recorded only under jev-version-1, with no refusal.
findings.expected: Repetition/stability attribution preserves the served model identity; different versions are not one unchanged-model sample.
findings.suggested_minimal_change: Require consistent served-model/state identities before aggregation, or partition/refuse mixed-version evaluations with explicit receipts.
findings.limits: The served-version change is mocked; no claim that the current provider changed versions during a live run.

findings.title: Nonfinite history metadata passes structural validation then fails cache serialization
findings.observed: validation_errors() returns empty; PredictionCache.key_for raises ValueError.
findings.expected: Invalid non-JSON inputs are rejected by validation before cache lookup/prediction, with a named request failure.
findings.suggested_minimal_change: Recursively validate supported JSON history values before serialization; keep unsupported backend history modes refused.
findings.limits: Invalid input is not a scientific query; this does not establish history-conditioned model support.

findings.title: The dated default log directory is a fixed historical date
findings.expected: A dated default follows an explicit local execution-date policy or is described as a fixed compatibility directory.
findings.suggested_minimal_change: Make the execution-date convention explicit and preserve existing frozen logs; do not rewrite historical artifacts.

regression.scope: Existing focused contracts; uncovered defect cases remain open.

cleanup.candidate: Small shared provider decoding/envelope normalization, because both existing transport loops duplicate the same failure; retain provider-specific retries/refusals/accounting.

evidence_boundary: All judgments and predictions remain planning-only model_prediction; deterministic contracts retain measurement, premise and terminal authority.
